en: The Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha on the Great King of Teachings for Subduing All *Guhya* Families: The Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, Volume One.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Chao San Da Fu, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial.
The body of great power, truly transformed, A vast body, firm and capable of shattering others;
Like the sun blazing intensely at the end of an eon, The Bodhisattva’s halo is likewise.
A pure ocean of jewels of merit, He dwells skillfully within the Buddha-fields.
At that time, with a single-minded devotion, I take refuge and pay homage to the Supreme King who subdues the bhūtas.
Then the Buddha addressed Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva, the Lord of the Three Realms,
and spoke the method for accomplishing the Great King of Teachings for Subduing All Bhūtas.
Then Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva said:
"If there are those who maintain and recite this,
seeking the methods for accomplishment..."
On the banks of two rivers, or in a śmaśāna forest,
or beneath a great tree, or within a palace of a noble being,
or inside the palace of the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi.
In such places as these, the rites performed will certainly achieve accomplishment.
If the bhūtas do not grant accomplishment within a single moment,
I shall go there myself and destroy those bhūtas.
At that time, Maheśvara joined his palms and,
bowing his head to the feet [of the Bodhisattva], addressed the Bodhisattva,
saying: "For my sake, please explain this secret mantra of the wrathful lord Mahāvajrapāṇi, which slays all bhūtas."
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi praised him, saying:
"Excellent, excellent! You have been able to request me to explain that secret method for subduing all bhūtas."
I shall now speak its mantra:
Oṃ vajrajvāle hana hana sarvabuddhān hūṃ phaṭ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, having spoken this mantra, [remained silent].
From the pores of his body, countless vajra-flames burst forth;
as those flames emerge, all the bhūtas and their retinues have their bodies completely withered and dried up, and they meet their death.
All the devas, Śakras, Brahmās, Nārāyaṇas, and others likewise met their end.
All the Tathāgatas were struck with wonder and simultaneously cried out:
"Excellent, excellent! O Great Auspicious One, Vajrapāṇi, Lord of the Three Realms!"
During the final age of the Tathāgata’s Dharma,
he will be well able to subdue all bhūtas and their retinues.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi—
Furthermore, the secret mantra of nectar is taught, which causes all bhūtas to quickly regain their lives.
The mantra is: Oṃ vajrayuṣṭi sara sara śami. At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this mantra.
From his own arm, he emits a wind of great nectar that enters the bodies of all the bhūtas and their retinues;
they immediately regain life, rise from the ground, and tremble with terror.
Seeing the Great Bodhisattva’s majestic power blazing intensely,
he cried out to the Bodhisattva, "Save me!
At that time, Mahāpatirāja Aparājita—
They also raised their joined palms, bowed their heads at his feet,
and addressed the Bodhisattva, saying:
"We pray that you will deign to show us compassion and protect us."
The Bodhisattva addressed them, saying: "You bhūtas and your retinues,
by following my Dharma teachings and benefiting all sentient beings,
I shall immediately save you."
All sentient beings within Jambudvīpa throughout the realms of the four great continents shall achieve success in all their ritual practices and recitations.
The sought-after holy medicines and holy jewels,
or gold, silver, pearls, lapis lazuli, padmarāga gems, and sūryakānta gems.
"Vajrakrandi, provide the most excellent food,
drink, clothing, fine incense, flowers, and so forth, all in abundance.
The bhūta replied, "It shall be so for whoever performs this rite and recites [the mantra]."
"I shall provide you with an abundance of such rare treasures as described above,
and I shall also personally attend to, serve, and make offerings to you.
The Bodhisattva replied, "If one upholds this teaching of all the Tathāgatas..."
They shall obtain and enjoy all necessary incense, flowers, clothing, and various precious gems.
Furthermore, the bhūtas said: "Whatever fear of kings, fear of enemies, and even fear of tigers, wolves, lions, and the like [shall be dispelled]."
He causes them all to be liberated and free from all obstacles.
The Bodhisattva spoke again: "O Great Lords of the Invincible Multitude, listen attentively!
Regarding all sentient beings who are indolent in the final age..."
For those who have broken their precepts, those who commit evil deeds, those who utter great falsehoods, and so forth—
may all the rites they perform be brought to fulfillment.
If they are not fulfilled, then you, O Bhūta-woman and Devī-woman, [shall suffer].
Nāga girls, yakṣī girls, asurī girls, kinnarī girls, mahoragī girls, and garuḍī girls.
As for the piśācī women, gandharvī women, and others,
I shall cause their heads and eyes to be shattered by the Great Vajra of Non-emptiness;
they shall swiftly meet their end and fall into the eight great hells.
At that time, all the Tathāgatas praised him, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, Vajrapāṇi!
You have brought great benefit to all sentient beings of future ages."
Excellent is the Great Bodhisattva Amoghasiddhi’s great power of diligence;
excellent is his turning of all wheels of Dharma to eliminate all suffering through various vast ritual procedures.
The method for accomplishing the mudrās, mantras, paṭas, and images.
At that time, Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva further spoke the mantra for restoring life, saying:
Oṃ kṛta kṛta kara kara mṛtāñjīvaya hṛīḥ. Having spoken this mantra...
All the devas and humans were then bewildered and fell to the ground;
overcome by great terror and trembling,
they rose from the earth and said to the Bodhisattva, "Save us, O Mahādeva!"
At that time, Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva comforted him, saying:
"Do not fear, do not fear."
"I have taught this for you in order to subdue the lords of the bhūtas and to cause all devas and humans to feel reverence and affection.
At that time, all the devas and goddesses also spoke these words.
"Vajrapāṇi, Great Lord of Wrathful Ones, save me! Save me!
The Bodhisattva replied, "O goddesses, if hereafter there be anyone who upholds my Dharma, I shall cause them to swiftly attain accomplishment."
"One should provide service, as well as gold, silver, lapis lazuli,
pearls, precious jewels, *padmarāga* gems, and all other such wealth.
Then, the goddesses, celestial maidens, and yakṣī maidens all raised their voices and said:
In future ages, if there be those who uphold the Dharma of the Bodhisattvas,
we shall serve them and provide all the wealth and treasures they may seek.
"If you disobey my instructions and do not serve me, I shall cause your entire lineage to be utterly destroyed.
The Bodhisattva spoke again: "If you disobey my teaching, you will be slandering all the Tathāgatas."
"You and all the leaders of the bhūtas shall have your heads and eyes destroyed;
you will immediately meet your end and fall into the eight great hells.
At that time, Vajrapāṇi, the Great Wrathful Lord, praised him, saying:
Excellent, excellent, you daughters!
In the future age of the final dharma,
if there should be anyone who receives and upholds this, [you shall protect them].
They personally guarded, served, and made offerings to him.
At that time, there was also the invincible Mahābhūta-lord and his retinue;
they all rose from their seats and joined their palms before him.
Having prostrated at the feet of that Great Wrathful Lord Vajrapāṇi,
he spoke the mantra of his own essential heart:

Oṃ śrī-mahā-bhūta-kula-sūḍani hūṃ oṃ | Oṃ śrī-vijaya-sūḍani hrīḥ oṃ | Oṃ śrī-vimala-sūḍani āḥ oṃ | Oṃ śrī-rati-sūḍani vaḥ oṃ | Oṃ śrī-manohara-sūḍani viḥ oṃ | Oṃ śrī-dhavalaka-sūḍani maṃ oṃ | Oṃ śrī-cakravartī-sūḍani teḥ || This mantra subsumes such great lords of the bhūtas.
It can bestow wealth, honor, and auspiciousness upon those who maintain this recitation.
At that time, he further taught the method for accomplishing the Kinnarī;
if one maintains this recitation, even for a brief moment, one will swiftly attain accomplishment.
Furthermore, by reciting the name of the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi,
all bhūtas and their retinues will come to serve him, acting like handmaidens.
The Bodhisattva spoke again:
"If you and your retinues do not rely upon my samādhi,
I shall cause all of you and your followers to be utterly destroyed."
Then the Lord of the Great Division of Aparājita addressed the Bodhisattva, saying:
"From this day forth, we shall all abide by the samādhi of the Bodhisattva;
may all those in the world who maintain and recite [this] attain accomplishment."
If [the rite] is obstructed and its purpose is not accomplished,
our clans will swiftly meet with destruction,
and we shall further incur the great sin of violating the samaya of all Tathāgatas.
May the Wrathful Vajra shatter my head!
After my life ends, may I fall into the eight great hells!

Furthermore, it is said that there are eight supreme places for the accomplishment of the lords of the bhūtas:
either on a riverbank, or in a śmaśāna,
or within the palace of the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi.
When this rite is performed,
all the bhūta women and others will certainly come together;
they will grant accomplishment, free from any further doubt.
Furthermore, the method for accomplishing the mudrā is taught:
form a firm fist with the left hand and extend the middle finger.
This mudrā is used for invocation and offering.
It causes the supreme multitude to swiftly grant accomplishment.
Joining both hands into fists and extending the index fingers—
this mudrā enables the holder of samādhi.
To swiftly grant accomplishment to the *bhūta* women,
form a firm fist with the left hand and extend the little finger.
This mudrā causes all *bhūtas* to appear before one and bestow accomplishment.
Again, extend the left hand with the index finger curved like a hook and press down upon the thumb;
this mudrā can subdue all bhūtas.
Then, extend the index and ring fingers of the left hand.
This can hook all bhūtas and eliminate all māras.
Forming a fist with the left hand and extending the thumb,
this mudrā can cause all bhūta women to appear before one.
Form a fist with the right hand and extend the little finger.
This is the *samaya-mudrā* of the *bhūta-kanyā*,
which can accomplish all tasks.
Extend both hands; place the right hand at the side of the waist and the left hand upon the right shoulder.
This is the supreme root-heart mahāmudrā of all ḍākinīs.
By binding this mudrā, one causes all ḍākinīs to swiftly appear before one.

"If there is any bhūta woman who does not abide by my samaya..."

Hūṃ phaṭ. Recite it thus eight hundred times.

*samayatiṣṭhadhu bhūtānāṃ samayamudrāṇa krodhārjita samājñāpayata pramuñcadhu svāhā | oṃ amogha-vajra kuśala kara kara kuru kuru hūṃ jaḥ*. When reciting this mantra:
Having bound this Vajrāṅkuśa mudrā, extend the two index fingers; this is the mudrā for dispatching the noble deities.
This concludes the third ritual procedure for dispatching the noble deities from the Great King of Teachings for Subduing All Classes [of Beings].
